concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw
import Lax342547.ProfileCounting
import Lax342547.CoordinateCounts

/-!
---
title: The finite simultaneous unary mixer estimate
type: lemma
---
The union runs only over nonzero bounded-rank profiles, tags, and labels.
All non-Z fixings are already covered by each individual bad event.
The finite estimate gives a simultaneous choice whenever its explicit
upper bound is below one. No unit law appears in that choice.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UnaryMixers

open Lax342547.MomentSpace Lax342547.TagGeometry Lax342547.ConcreteGeometry
open Lax342547.ConcreteCut Lax342547.CutProfiles Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw

abbrev Test (k n b degree K : ℕ) :=
  {x : Profile k n b degree // ∑ e, (x.val e).rank ≤ K} × Tag k × (Fin b → Binary)

noncomputable instance (k n b degree K : ℕ) : Fintype (Test k n b degree K) := Fintype.ofFinite _

def Good {k n b degree r₀ J : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) (K s₀ : ℕ)
    (M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Profile k n b degree, x ≠ 0 → (∑ e, (x.val e).rank ≤ K) →
    ∀ l s, ¬ UnaryBad D x l s s₀ M

def UniformUnary {k n b degree r₀ J : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) (K s₀ : ℕ)
    (M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Profile k n b degree, x ≠ 0 → (∑ e, (x.val e).rank ≤ K) → ∀ l s,
    ∃ W : Submodule Binary (Module.Dual Binary (Fin n → Binary)),
      Module.finrank Binary W ≤ 4 * J * (2 * k) * K ∧
      ∀ z : Base k n → Binary, ∀ hz : ∀ i, i ∉ allowedBase k n l → z i = 0,
        2 * (J - s₀) ≤ (FormalQuadratic.polarMatrix (fun v =>
          gradient D (leftMixers M) (rightMixers M) x (UnaryMixer.atomAlongZ l s z hz v))).rank ∧
        ∀ u v, (∀ a ∈ W, a u = a v) →
          gradient D (leftMixers M) (rightMixers M) x (UnaryMixer.atomAlongZ l s z hz u) =
            gradient D (leftMixers M) (rightMixers M) x (UnaryMixer.atomAlongZ l s z hz v)

noncomputable def testCountBound (k n b degree K : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((K + 1) ^ Fintype.card (Component (Tag k)) *
    2 ^ (Fintype.card (Coordinate k n b degree) * K + K * K)) * (2 * k + 1) * 2 ^ b

open scoped ENNReal

noncomputable def failureBound (k n b degree J K s₀ : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  testCountBound k n b degree K *
    (2 ^ (2 * J * K ^ 2 + (s₀ + 1) * (4 * J * (2 * k) * K)) / 2 ^ ((s₀ + 1) * n))

noncomputable def threshold (k b degree J K s₀ : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (K + 1) ^ Fintype.card (Component (Tag k)) * (2 * k + 1) * 2 ^ b *
    2 ^ ((∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * K + K * K +
      (2 * J * K ^ 2 + (s₀ + 1) * (4 * J * (2 * k) * K)))

axiom failureBound_le_geometric (k n b degree J K s₀ : ℕ)
    (hmargin : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 3) * K ≤ s₀) :
    failureBound k n b degree J K s₀ ≤ (threshold k b degree J K s₀ : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 ^ n

axiom uniform_of_good {k n b degree r₀ J K s₀ : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr)
    (M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree)
    (hM : Good D K s₀ M) : UniformUnary D K s₀ M

axiom failureBound_lt_one (k n b degree J K s₀ : ℕ)
    (hmargin : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 3) * K ≤ s₀)
    (hn : threshold k b degree J K s₀ ≤ n) :
    failureBound k n b degree J K s₀ < 1

axiom simultaneous_failure_bound {k n b degree r₀ J K : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (hk : 0 < k) (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) (s₀ : ℕ) :
    (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree)).toOuterMeasure
      {M | ¬ Good D K s₀ M} ≤ failureBound k n b degree J K s₀

axiom exists_of_failureBound_lt_one {k n b degree r₀ J K : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (hk : 0 < k) (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) (s₀ : ℕ)
    (hsmall : failureBound k n b degree J K s₀ < 1) :
    ∃ M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree, Good D K s₀ M

axiom exists_for_large_n (k b degree J K s₀ : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k)
    (hmargin : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 3) * K ≤ s₀) :
    ∃ n₀, ∀ n, n₀ ≤ n → ∀ r₀ (hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n)
      (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr),
      ∃ M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree, Good D K s₀ M

axiom exists_uniform_unary (k b degree J K s₀ : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k)
    (hmargin : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 3) * K ≤ s₀) :
    ∃ n₀, ∀ n, n₀ ≤ n → ∀ r₀ (hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n)
      (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr),
      ∃ M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree, UniformUnary D K s₀ M

end Lax342547.UnaryMixers

concepts.title: Joint distribution of the unary mixer row matrix
concepts.description:
All indexed L and R matrices are sampled from one finite product.
The full forward/reverse observation list has additive compatibility
cost. A surjective coordinate selection retains just the incident
formal rows, including their separate L and R halves.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.UnaryMixer
import Lax342547.MixerRowLaw
import Lax342547.CorankCounting

/-!
---
title: Joint distribution of the unary mixer row matrix
type: lemma
---
All indexed L and R matrices are sampled from one finite product.
The full forward/reverse observation list has additive compatibility
cost. A surjective coordinate selection retains just the incident
formal rows, including their separate L and R halves.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw

open Lax342547.MomentSpace Lax342547.UnaryMixer

variable {E I N : Type} [Fintype E] [Fintype I] [Fintype N]

abbrev Index (E : Type) (J : ℕ) := Bool × Fin J × E × E

abbrev RowIndex (r : E → ℕ) (inc : Finset E) (J : ℕ) :=
  (t : Block inc J) × (Fin (blockRank r t) ⊕ Fin (blockRank r t))

noncomputable instance (r : E → ℕ) (inc : Finset E) (J : ℕ) :
    DecidableEq (RowIndex r inc J) := Classical.decEq _

noncomputable instance (r : E → ℕ) (inc : Finset E) (J : ℕ) :
    Fintype (RowIndex r inc J) := Fintype.ofFinite _

def flatten {r : E → ℕ} {inc : Finset E} {J : ℕ} :
    Rows r inc J ≃ₗ[Binary] (RowIndex r inc J → Binary) where
  toFun x a := Sum.elim (x a.1).1 (x a.1).2 a.2
  invFun y t := (fun a => y ⟨t, .inl a⟩, fun a => y ⟨t, .inr a⟩)
  left_inv x := rfl
  right_inv y := by funext a; rcases a with ⟨t, a | a⟩ <;> rfl
  map_add' x y := by funext a; rcases a with ⟨t, a | a⟩ <;> rfl
  map_smul' a x := by funext b; rcases b with ⟨t, b | b⟩ <;> rfl

abbrev FullList (r : E → ℕ) (J : ℕ) (N : Type) :=
  ∀ p : Index E J, Matrix (Fin (r p.2.2.1)) N Binary × Matrix N (Fin (r p.2.2.2)) Binary

def fullObservations {r : E → ℕ} {J : ℕ}
    (Z : ∀ e, Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Binary) (D : Matrix I N Binary) :
    (Index E J → Matrix I I Binary) →ₗ[Binary] FullList r J N :=
  FiniteLinearLaw.familyMap (fun p => MixerRowLaw.observations (Z p.2.2.1) (Z p.2.2.2) D)

def pack {r : E → ℕ} (inc : Finset E) {J : ℕ} :
    FullList r J N →ₗ[Binary] Matrix (RowIndex r inc J) N Binary where
  toFun y a i := match a with
    | ⟨.inl (j, e, f), .inl h⟩ => (y (false, j, e, f.val)).1 h i
    | ⟨.inl (j, e, f), .inr h⟩ => (y (true, j, e, f.val)).1 h i
    | ⟨.inr (j, e, f), .inl h⟩ => (y (false, j, e.val, f)).2 i h
    | ⟨.inr (j, e, f), .inr h⟩ => (y (true, j, e.val, f)).2 i h
  map_add' x y := by
    funext a i
    rcases a with ⟨⟨j, e, f⟩ | ⟨j, e, f⟩, a | a⟩ <;> rfl
  map_smul' c x := by
    funext a i
    rcases a with ⟨⟨j, e, f⟩ | ⟨j, e, f⟩, a | a⟩ <;> rfl

def mixerRows {r : E → ℕ} (inc : Finset E) {J : ℕ}
    (Z : ∀ e, Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Binary) (D : Matrix I N Binary) :
    (Index E J → Matrix I I Binary) →ₗ[Binary] Matrix (RowIndex r inc J) N Binary :=
  (pack inc).comp (fullObservations Z D)

noncomputable def rowLinear {r : E → ℕ} (inc : Finset E) {J : ℕ}
    (Z : ∀ e, Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Binary) (D : Matrix I N Binary)
    (M : Index E J → Matrix I I Binary) : (N → Binary) →ₗ[Binary] Rows r inc J :=
  (rowMap inc Z (fun j e f => M (false, j, e, f))
    (fun j e f => M (true, j, e, f))).comp D.mulVecLin

axiom mixerRows_rank {r : E → ℕ} (inc : Finset E) {J : ℕ}
    (Z : ∀ e, Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Binary) (D : Matrix I N Binary)
    (M : Index E J → Matrix I I Binary) :
    (mixerRows inc Z D M).rank = Module.finrank Binary (LinearMap.range (rowLinear inc Z D M))

open scoped ENNReal

axiom joint_row_law [DecidableEq E] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq N]
    {r : E → ℕ} (inc : Finset E) {J K : ℕ}
    (Z : ∀ e, Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Binary) (D : Matrix I N Binary)
    (hZ : ∀ e, Function.Injective (Z e).mulVec) (hD : Function.Injective D.mulVec)
    (hr : ∑ e, r e ≤ K) (y : Matrix (RowIndex r inc J) N Binary) :
    (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Index E J → Matrix I I Binary)).map (mixerRows inc Z D) y ≤
      2 ^ (2 * J * K ^ 2) * PMF.uniformOfFintype (Matrix (RowIndex r inc J) N Binary) y

axiom row_corank_bound [DecidableEq E] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq N]
    {r : E → ℕ} (inc : Finset E) {J K : ℕ}
    (Z : ∀ e, Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Binary) (D : Matrix I N Binary)
    (hZ : ∀ e, Function.Injective (Z e).mulVec) (hD : Function.Injective D.mulVec)
    (hr : ∑ e, r e ≤ K) (s : ℕ) :
    (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Index E J → Matrix I I Binary)).toOuterMeasure
      {M | (mixerRows inc Z D M).rank + s ≤ Fintype.card (RowIndex r inc J)} ≤
        (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (2 * J * K ^ 2 + s * (4 * J * inc.card * K)) / 2 ^ (s * Fintype.card N)

def leftMixers {J : ℕ} (M : Index E J → Matrix I I Binary) : Fin J → E → E → Matrix I I Binary :=
  fun j e f => M (false, j, e, f)

def rightMixers {J : ℕ} (M : Index E J → Matrix I I Binary) : Fin J → E → E → Matrix I I Binary :=
  fun j e f => M (true, j, e, f)

open Lax342547.TagGeometry Lax342547.ConcreteGeometry Lax342547.ConcreteCut Lax342547.CutProfiles

def UnaryBad {k n b degree r₀ J : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) (x : Profile k n b degree)
    (l : Tag k) (s : Fin b → Binary) (s₀ : ℕ)
    (M : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree) : Prop :=
  ∃ z : Base k n → Binary, ∃ hz : ∀ i, i ∉ allowedBase k n l → z i = 0,
    (FormalQuadratic.polarMatrix (fun v =>
      gradient D (leftMixers M) (rightMixers M) x (atomAlongZ l s z hz v))).rank < 2 * (J - s₀)

axiom unary_failure_probability {k n b degree r₀ J K : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n}
    (hk : 0 < k) (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr)
    (x : Profile k n b degree) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hK : ∑ e, (x.val e).rank ≤ K)
    (l : Tag k) (s : Fin b → Binary) (s₀ : ℕ) :
    (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree)).toOuterMeasure
      {M | UnaryBad D x l s s₀ M} ≤
        (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (2 * J * K ^ 2 + (s₀ + 1) * (4 * J * (2 * k) * K)) / 2 ^ ((s₀ + 1) * n)

end Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw

joint_row_law : ∀ {E I N : Type} [inst : Fintype E] [inst_1 : Fintype I] [inst_2 : Fintype N] [inst_3 : DecidableEq E]
  [inst_4 : DecidableEq I] [inst_5 : DecidableEq N] {r : E → Nat} (inc : Finset E) {J K : Nat}
  (Z : (e : E) → Matrix I (Fin (r e)) Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary) (D : Matrix I N Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary),
  (∀ (e : E), Function.Injective (Z e).mulVec) →
    Function.Injective D.mulVec →
      instLENat.le (Finset.univ.sum fun e => r e) K →
        ∀ (y : Matrix (Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw.RowIndex r inc J) N Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary),
          ENNReal.instLE.le
            (PMF.instFunLike.coe
              (PMF.map (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe (Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw.mixerRows inc Z D))
                (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw.Index E J → Matrix I I Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary)))
              y)

concepts.description:
Lemma 5.5: one choice of all indexed L,R matrices and all sharp M matrices

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.UnaryMixers
import Lax342547.BinaryMixers

/-!
---
title: Uniform mixing forms chosen simultaneously before any unit law
type: lemma
---
Lemma 5.5: one choice of all indexed L,R matrices and all sharp M matrices
has the unary polar-rank and bounded-row-space properties and every binary
parity rank bound. An explicit threshold in n pays for both finite unions.
The paper's displayed mixer parameters satisfy the required margin.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UniformMixers

open Lax342547.MomentSpace Lax342547.TagGeometry Lax342547.ConcreteGeometry
open Lax342547.ConcreteCut Lax342547.CutProfiles Lax342547.UnaryRowLaw

noncomputable def threshold (k b degree J K s₀ : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  max 50 (UnaryMixers.threshold k b degree J K s₀ +
    2 ^ (2 * b + 2 * Fintype.card (Index (Component (Tag k)) J)) + 2 ^ (2 * b + 2))

def paperS₀ (k b degree K : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  40 * (K + 1) * (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 5)

def paperJ (k b degree K : ℕ) : ℕ := 101 * (paperS₀ k b degree K + K ^ 2 + 1)

axiom exists_uniform_mixers (k b degree J K s₀ : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (hd : 1 ≤ degree)
    (hmargin : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 3) * K ≤ s₀)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : threshold k b degree J K s₀ ≤ n)
    (r₀ : ℕ) (hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n) (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) :
    ∃ L : Index (Component (Tag k)) J → Moment k n b degree,
      ∃ M : Fin b → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Binary,
        UnaryMixers.UniformUnary D K s₀ L ∧ BinaryMixers.UniformBinary hr hd L M

axiom paper_parameters (k b degree K : ℕ) :
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (degree + 1), b.choose j) * ((2 * k + 1) ^ 2 + 3) * K ≤ paperS₀ k b degree K ∧
      100 * (paperS₀ k b degree K + K ^ 2 + 1) < paperJ k b degree K

axiom exists_paper_mixers (k b degree K : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (hd : 1 ≤ degree) :
    ∃ n₀, ∀ n, n₀ ≤ n → ∀ r₀ (hr : 2 * r₀ ≤ n)
      (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr),
      ∃ L : Index (Component (Tag k)) (paperJ k b degree K) → Moment k n b degree,
        ∃ M : Fin b → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Binary,
          UnaryMixers.UniformUnary D K (paperS₀ k b degree K) L ∧ BinaryMixers.UniformBinary hr hd L M

end Lax342547.UniformMixers

    (K Cs : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ h : ℕ,∀ c : ℕ,∃ N₀ : ℕ,∀ N p m : ℕ,N₀ ≤ N → p ≤ N/8 → m ≤ N/100 →
      ∀ (U I : Type) [Fintype U] [Fintype I] (E : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Binary)
      [Nonempty (Frame (Fin p) (Fin h) (Fin N) E)]
      (ρ : U → ℝ) (P : U → Pin (Comp × Bool) (Fin 2 × (Fin p ⊕ Fin h)) (Fin N))
      (A : U → Fin 2 → Comp → Frame (Fin p) (Fin h) (Fin N) E)
      (accept : U → U → Prop) (CL CR : I → U → Prop) (keyL keyR : U → I)
      (T : ∀ a b,Table (P a) (P b)) (M : ℝ),
      Probability ρ → 0 ≤ M → M ≤ (2 : ℝ)^m →
      (Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ)^(Cs*N) →
      (∀ u,(P u).rank ≤ K) →

import Lax342547.EntropyContainers
import Lax342547.TerminalCuts

/-!
---
title: Terminal containers for actual admissible unit laws
type: lemma
---
The entropy container family applies to the actual marginal and pair capacity constraints. Every terminal container has the vertex and pair exceptions of Lemma 3.3, with the explicit fingerprint count and no injectivity restriction on later sampled raw types.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UnitContainers

open Lax342547.RelativeEntropy Lax342547.UnitLaws Lax342547.ContainerLaws
open Lax342547.RetainedImages Lax342547.CellAveraging

axiom residual_feasible_iff {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R₀ : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ) (R : Finset (Ω × Ω)) (ρ : Ω × Ω → ℝ) :
    ρ ∈ residual {σ | Feasible μ R₀ M κ σ} R ↔
      Feasible μ (fun x y => R₀ x y ∧ (x,y) ∈ R) M κ ρ

axiom terminal_unit_exceptions {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R₀ : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ) (R : Finset (Ω × Ω))
    (hμ : ∀ x, 0 ≤ μ x) (hM : 0 < M) (hκ : 0 < κ)
    (hn : ¬ (residual {σ | Feasible μ R₀ M κ σ} R).Nonempty) :
    ∃ S : Ω → Prop, ∃ E : Ω → Ω → Prop,
      cellMass μ S < 1/M ∧ pairEventMass μ μ E < 1/κ ∧
      (∀ x y, R₀ x y → (x,y) ∈ R → S x ∨ S y ∨ E x y)

axiom unit_container_family {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R₀ : Ω → Ω → Prop) (H : (Ω × Ω) → (Ω × Ω) → Prop)
    (M κ ε : ℝ) (L : ℕ) (hμ : Probability μ) (hμpos : ∀ x, 0 < μ x)
    (hM : 0 < M) (hκ : 0 < κ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1)
    (hL : Real.log κ/(-Real.log (1-ε))+1 ≤ L)
    (hsuper : ∀ ρ, Feasible μ R₀ M κ ρ → ε ≤ conflictMass ρ H) :
    ∃ C : Finset (Finset (Ω × Ω)),
      C.card ≤ (Fintype.card Ω^2+1)^L ∧
      (∀ R ∈ C, ∃ S : Ω → Prop, ∃ E : Ω → Ω → Prop,
        cellMass μ S < 1/M ∧ pairEventMass μ μ E < 1/κ ∧
        (∀ x y, R₀ x y → (x,y) ∈ R → S x ∨ S y ∨ E x y)) ∧
      (∀ I : Finset (Ω × Ω), (∀ x ∈ I, ∀ y ∈ I, ¬ H x y) → ∃ R ∈ C, I ⊆ R)

end Lax342547.UnitContainers

  (ρ : Prod Ω Ω → Real),
  Iff
    (Set.instMembership.mem
      (Lax342547.ContainerLaws.residual (Set.ofPred fun σ => Lax342547.UnitLaws.Feasible μ R₀ M κ σ) R) ρ)

                (And (Real.instLT.lt (Lax342547.CellAveraging.pairEventMass μ μ E) (instHDiv.hDiv 1 κ))

                          (∀ (x : Prod Ω Ω),

                                ∀ (y : Prod Ω Ω), SetLike.instMembership.mem I y → Not (H x y)) →
                            Exists fun R => And (SetLike.instMembership.mem C R) (Finset.instPartialOrder.le I R)))

concepts.title: Admissible pair laws
concepts.description: Compactness, convexity and entropy minimization for the actual marginal and pair capacity constraints.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.EntropyProjection
import Lax342547.PairRecovery

/-!
---
title: Admissible pair laws
type: lemma
---
Compactness, convexity and entropy minimization for the actual marginal and pair capacity constraints.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UnitLaws

open Lax342547.RelativeEntropy
open scoped BigOperators

def Feasible {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω] (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R : Ω → Ω → Prop)
    (M κ : ℝ) (ρ : Ω × Ω → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Probability ρ ∧ (∀ x, (∑ y, ρ (x,y)) ≤ M*μ x) ∧
    (∀ y, (∑ x, ρ (x,y)) ≤ M*μ y) ∧
    (∀ xy, ρ xy ≤ κ*(μ xy.1*μ xy.2)) ∧ (∀ xy, ¬ R xy.1 xy.2 → ρ xy = 0)

axiom feasible_closed {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ) : IsClosed {ρ | Feasible μ R M κ ρ}

axiom feasible_compact {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ) : IsCompact {ρ | Feasible μ R M κ ρ}

axiom feasible_convex {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ) : Convex ℝ {ρ | Feasible μ R M κ ρ}

axiom entropy_minimizer {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ)
    (hne : ∃ ρ, Feasible μ R M κ ρ) :
    ∃ ρ, Feasible μ R M κ ρ ∧
      (∀ ρ', Feasible μ R M κ ρ' → entropy ρ (fun xy => μ xy.1*μ xy.2) ≤ entropy ρ' (fun xy => μ xy.1*μ xy.2)) ∧
      (∀ ρ', Feasible μ R M κ ρ' → ∀ xy, 0 < ρ' xy → 0 < ρ xy) ∧
      (∀ ρ', Feasible μ R M κ ρ' → entropy ρ' ρ ≤
        entropy ρ' (fun xy => μ xy.1*μ xy.2)-entropy ρ (fun xy => μ xy.1*μ xy.2))

axiom feasible_entropy_budget {Ω : Type} [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (R : Ω → Ω → Prop) (M κ : ℝ) (ρ : Ω × Ω → ℝ)
    (hμ : Probability μ) (hμpos : ∀ x, 0 < μ x) (hκ : 0 < κ) (hρ : Feasible μ R M κ ρ) :
    0 ≤ entropy ρ (fun xy => μ xy.1*μ xy.2) ∧ entropy ρ (fun xy => μ xy.1*μ xy.2) ≤ Real.log κ

end Lax342547.UnitLaws

  (Exists fun ρ => Lax342547.UnitLaws.Feasible μ R M κ ρ) →
    Exists fun ρ =>
      And (Lax342547.UnitLaws.Feasible μ R M κ ρ)
        (And
          (∀ (ρ' : Prod Ω Ω → Real),
            Lax342547.UnitLaws.Feasible μ R M κ ρ' →
              Real.instLE.le (Lax342547.RelativeEntropy.entropy ρ fun xy => instHMul.hMul (μ xy.fst) (μ xy.snd))
                (Lax342547.RelativeEntropy.entropy ρ' fun xy => instHMul.hMul (μ xy.fst) (μ xy.snd)))
          (And
            (∀ (ρ' : Prod Ω Ω → Real),
              Lax342547.UnitLaws.Feasible μ R M κ ρ' →
                ∀ (xy : Prod Ω Ω), Real.instLT.lt 0 (ρ' xy) → Real.instLT.lt 0 (ρ xy))

                Real.instLE.le (Lax342547.RelativeEntropy.entropy ρ' ρ)
                  (instHSub.hSub (Lax342547.RelativeEntropy.entropy ρ' fun xy => instHMul.hMul (μ xy.fst) (μ xy.snd))

              (Real.log κ))

/-!
---
title: Whole-unit conditioned pin avoidance
type: lemma
---
Pins inside actual primal images inherit raw span avoidance, including the exact conditioning cost for any retained accepted set.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UnitSpanAvoidance

open Lax342547.MomentSpace Lax342547.RelativeEntropy Lax342547.RetainedImages

axiom pin_intersection_is_primal_hit {B H N : Type} [Fintype B] [Fintype H] [Fintype N]
    {E : Matrix B B Binary} (F : Frame B H N E) (V W : Submodule Binary (N → Binary))
    (hV : V ≤ LinearMap.range F.P.mulVecLin) (hbad : ¬ Disjoint V W) :
    ∃ c : B → Binary,c ≠ 0 ∧ F.P.mulVec c ∈ W

axiom capped_unit_span_avoidance {A B H N : Type}
    [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Fintype H] [Fintype N] [DecidableEq B] [DecidableEq H] [DecidableEq N]
    (E : Matrix B B Binary) [Nonempty (Frame B H N E)]
    (α : A → ℝ) (image : A → Frame B H N E) (V : A → Submodule Binary (N → Binary))
    (W : Submodule Binary (N → Binary)) (M : ℝ) (hα : ∀ a,0 ≤ α a) (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (hN : Fintype.card B+Fintype.card H+1 ≤ Fintype.card N)
    (hV : ∀ a,V a ≤ LinearMap.range (image a).P.mulVecLin)
    (hcap : ∀ F,push α image F ≤ M*weights (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Frame B H N E)) F) :
    cellMass α (fun a => ¬ Disjoint (V a) W) ≤
      M*(2*((2 : ℝ)^(Fintype.card B+Fintype.card H+Module.finrank Binary W)/(2 : ℝ)^Fintype.card N))

axiom conditioned_unit_span_avoidance {A B H N : Type}
    [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Fintype H] [Fintype N] [DecidableEq B] [DecidableEq H] [DecidableEq N]
    (E : Matrix B B Binary) [Nonempty (Frame B H N E)]
    (α : A → ℝ) (image : A → Frame B H N E) (V : A → Submodule Binary (N → Binary))
    (W : Submodule Binary (N → Binary)) (C : A → Prop) (M τ : ℝ)
    (hα : ∀ a,0 ≤ α a) (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hτ : 0 < τ) (hC : τ ≤ cellMass α C)
    (hN : Fintype.card B+Fintype.card H+1 ≤ Fintype.card N)
    (hV : ∀ a,V a ≤ LinearMap.range (image a).P.mulVecLin)
    (hcap : ∀ F,push α image F ≤ M*weights (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Frame B H N E)) F) :
    cellMass (conditionalLaw α C) (fun a => ¬ Disjoint (V a) W) ≤
      (M/τ)*(2*((2 : ℝ)^(Fintype.card B+Fintype.card H+Module.finrank Binary W)/(2 : ℝ)^Fintype.card N))

end Lax342547.UnitSpanAvoidance

    Not (Disjoint V W) → Exists fun c => And (Ne c 0) (SetLike.instMembership.mem W (F.P.mulVec c))

concepts.title: Universal protected pin witnesses
concepts.description: Independent pin witnesses have an amplified probability bound even when the small protected space depends on the whole unit.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.IndependentWitnesses
import Lax342547.PhaseAverages

/-!
---
title: Universal protected pin witnesses
type: lemma
---
Independent pin witnesses have an amplified probability bound even when the small protected space depends on the whole unit.
-/

namespace Lax342547.UniversalWitnesses

open Lax342547.MomentSpace Lax342547.RetainedImages Lax342547.RealCellLaws Lax342547.PushforwardWalsh
open scoped BigOperators

axiom some_protected_witness_probability {I H N : Type}
    [Fintype I] [Fintype H] [Fintype N] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq H] [DecidableEq N]
    (V : I → Submodule Binary (N → Binary)) (hV : iSupIndep V)
    (K : ℕ) (hK : ∀ i,Module.finrank Binary (V i) ≤ K) :
    cellMass (weights (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Matrix N H Binary)))
      (fun Y => ∃ S : Submodule Binary (H → Binary),Module.finrank Binary S ≤ K ∧
        ∀ i,∃ v : V i,v.val ≠ 0 ∧ Y.transpose.mulVec v.val ∈ S) ≤
      (2 : ℝ)^(Fintype.card H*K+2*K*Fintype.card I)/(2 : ℝ)^(Fintype.card H*Fintype.card I)

axiom marked_unit_witness_probability {I H N B : Type}
    [Fintype I] [Fintype H] [Fintype N] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq H] [DecidableEq N]
    (V : I → Submodule Binary (N → Binary)) (hV : iSupIndep V)
    (β : B → ℝ) (Y : B → Matrix N H Binary) (S : B → Submodule Binary (H → Binary))
    (K : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hβ : ∀ b,0 ≤ β b) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hK : ∀ i,Module.finrank Binary (V i) ≤ K)
    (hS : ∀ b,Module.finrank Binary (S b) ≤ K)
    (hcap : ∀ y,push β Y y ≤ L*weights (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Matrix N H Binary)) y) :
    cellMass β (fun b => ∀ i,∃ v : V i,v.val ≠ 0 ∧ (Y b).transpose.mulVec v.val ∈ S b) ≤
      L*((2 : ℝ)^(Fintype.card H*K+2*K*Fintype.card I)/(2 : ℝ)^(Fintype.card H*Fintype.card I))

end Lax342547.UniversalWitnesses

      (∀ (b : B), Real.instLE.le 0 (β b)) →

concepts.title: Orthogonality and finite Walsh correlation bounds
concepts.description:
The real binary character is 1 on zero and -1 on one. Its dot-product
matrix has orthogonal rows. The resulting exact squared operator bound
controls correlations of bounded weights and subprobability masses.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.MomentSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sqrt
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Rank

/-!
---
title: Orthogonality and finite Walsh correlation bounds
type: lemma
---
The real binary character is 1 on zero and -1 on one. Its dot-product
matrix has orthogonal rows. The resulting exact squared operator bound
controls correlations of bounded weights and subprobability masses.
-/

namespace Lax342547.Walsh

open Lax342547.MomentSpace

noncomputable def sign (z : Binary) : ℝ := if z = 0 then 1 else -1

noncomputable def phase {I : Type} [Fintype I] (x y : I → Binary) : ℝ :=
  sign (dotProduct x y)

noncomputable def transform {I : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (f : (I → Binary) → ℝ) (x : I → Binary) : ℝ := ∑ y, phase x y * f y

axiom linear_orthogonality {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module Binary V] [Fintype V]
    (f : V →ₗ[Binary] Binary) (hf : f ≠ 0) : ∑ x, sign (f x) = 0

axiom orthogonality {I : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (x z : I → Binary) :
    ∑ y, phase x y * phase z y = if x = z then (2 : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card I else 0

axiom transform_energy {I : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (f : (I → Binary) → ℝ) :
    ∑ x, (transform f x) ^ 2 = (2 : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card I * ∑ y, (f y) ^ 2

axiom dot_correlation_sq {I : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (f g : (I → Binary) → ℝ) :
    (∑ x, ∑ y, f x * g y * phase x y) ^ 2 ≤
      (2 : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card I * (∑ x, (f x) ^ 2) * ∑ y, (g y) ^ 2

axiom subprobability_dot_bound {I : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (α β f g : (I → Binary) → ℝ) (p₁ p₂ : ℝ)
    (hα : ∀ x, 0 ≤ α x ∧ α x ≤ p₁) (hβ : ∀ y, 0 ≤ β y ∧ β y ≤ p₂)
    (hαsum : ∑ x, α x ≤ 1) (hβsum : ∑ y, β y ≤ 1)
    (hf : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ 1) (hg : ∀ y, |g y| ≤ 1) :
    |∑ x, ∑ y, α x * β y * f x * g y * phase x y| ≤
      Real.sqrt ((2 : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card I * p₁ * p₂)

end Lax342547.Walsh

statements.signature:
dot_correlation_sq : ∀ {I : Type} [inst : Fintype I] [inst_1 : DecidableEq I] (f g : (I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary) → Real),
  Real.instLE.le
    (instHPow.hPow
      (Finset.univ.sum fun x =>
        Finset.univ.sum fun y => instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (f x) (g y)) (Lax342547.Walsh.phase x y))
      2)
    (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow 2 (Fintype.card I)) (Finset.univ.sum fun x => instHPow.hPow (f x) 2))
      (Finset.univ.sum fun y => instHPow.hPow (g y) 2))

linear_orthogonality : ∀ {V : Type} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary V] [inst_2 : Fintype V]
  (f : LinearMap (RingHom.id Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary) V Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary),
  Ne f 0 → Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun x => Lax342547.Walsh.sign (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe f x)) 0

orthogonality : ∀ {I : Type} [inst : Fintype I] [inst_1 : DecidableEq I] (x z : I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary),
  Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun y => instHMul.hMul (Lax342547.Walsh.phase x y) (Lax342547.Walsh.phase z y))
    (ite (Eq x z) (instHPow.hPow 2 (Fintype.card I)) 0)

subprobability_dot_bound : ∀ {I : Type} [inst : Fintype I] [inst_1 : DecidableEq I] (α β f g : (I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary) → Real)
  (p₁ p₂ : Real),
  (∀ (x : I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary), And (Real.instLE.le 0 (α x)) (Real.instLE.le (α x) p₁)) →
    (∀ (y : I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary), And (Real.instLE.le 0 (β y)) (Real.instLE.le (β y) p₂)) →
      Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun x => α x) 1 →
        Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun y => β y) 1 →
          (∀ (x : I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary), Real.instLE.le (abs (f x)) 1) →
            (∀ (y : I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary), Real.instLE.le (abs (g y)) 1) →
              Real.instLE.le
                (abs
                  (Finset.univ.sum fun x =>
                    Finset.univ.sum fun y =>
                      instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (α x) (β y)) (f x)) (g y))
                        (Lax342547.Walsh.phase x y)))
                (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow 2 (Fintype.card I)) p₁) p₂).sqrt

transform_energy : ∀ {I : Type} [inst : Fintype I] [inst_1 : DecidableEq I] (f : (I → Lax342547.MomentSpace.Binary) → Real),
  Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun x => instHPow.hPow (Lax342547.Walsh.transform f x) 2)
    (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow 2 (Fintype.card I)) (Finset.univ.sum fun y => instHPow.hPow (f y) 2))

concepts.title: Witness atoms and their numerical tester records
concepts.description:
A witness atom includes an actual allowed base vector and selector label.
Its numerical record keeps only the tag and tester summary. These records
determine the tester part of every atom-pair gradient entry.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax342547.Atoms
import Lax342547.BinaryPrescriptions

/-!
---
title: Witness atoms and their numerical tester records
type: lemma
---
A witness atom includes an actual allowed base vector and selector label.
Its numerical record keeps only the tag and tester summary. These records
determine the tester part of every atom-pair gradient entry.
-/

namespace Lax342547.WitnessAtoms

open Lax342547.MomentSpace Lax342547.TagGeometry Lax342547.ConcreteGeometry
open Lax342547.ConcreteCut Lax342547.Atoms

structure PointAtom (k n b degree : ℕ) where
  tag : Tag k
  label : Fin b → Binary
  base : Base k n → Binary
  supported : ∀ i, i ∉ allowedBase k n tag → base i = 0

def PointAtom.vector {k n b degree : ℕ} (x : PointAtom k n b degree) : Vector k n b degree :=
  point selectorEval x.label x.base

noncomputable def PointAtom.profile {k n b degree : ℕ} (x : PointAtom k n b degree) :
    Profile k n b degree := atom x.tag x.label x.base x.supported

structure Numerical (k : ℕ) where
  tag : Tag k
  summary : Option (Tag k × Tag k) → Binary

def PointAtom.numerical {k n b degree r : ℕ} (hr : 2 * r ≤ n) (x : PointAtom k n b degree) :
    Numerical k := ⟨x.tag, testerSummary (degree := degree) hr x.label x.base⟩

def Numerical.aTag {k : ℕ} (x : Numerical k) (t : Tag k) : Binary :=
  ∑ d, x.summary (some (d, t))

def Numerical.bTag {k : ℕ} (x : Numerical k) (t : Tag k) : Binary :=
  if x.tag = t then 0 else x.summary none

def Numerical.role {k : ℕ} (x : Numerical k) : Binary := ∑ t, x.aTag t

def testerEntry {k : ℕ} (x y : Numerical k) : Binary :=
  x.role * y.role + ∑ t, (x.aTag t * y.bTag t + x.bTag t * y.aTag t)

abbrev ProductIndex (k J : ℕ) := Fin J × Lax342547.CutProfiles.Component (Tag k) ×
  Lax342547.CutProfiles.Component (Tag k)

def allowedIndex {k J : ℕ} (x y : Numerical k) (t : ProductIndex k J) : Prop :=
  x.tag ∈ t.2.1.val ∧ y.tag ∈ t.2.2.val

axiom tester_properties {k : ℕ} :
    (∀ x y : Numerical k, testerEntry x y = testerEntry y x) ∧
      ∀ x : Numerical k, testerEntry x x = x.role

axiom atom_testers {k n b degree r : ℕ} {hr : 2 * r ≤ n}
    (D : Testers (k := k) (b := b) (degree := degree) hr) (x : PointAtom k n b degree) :
    D.role x.profile = (x.numerical hr).role ∧
      (∀ t, D.aTag t x.profile = (x.numerical hr).aTag t) ∧
      ∀ t, D.bTag t x.profile = (x.numerical hr).bTag t

axiom allowed_index {k J : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hJ : 0 < J) (x y : Numerical k) :
    ∃ t : ProductIndex k J, allowedIndex x y t

end Lax342547.WitnessAtoms

statements.signature:
allowed_index : ∀ {k J : Nat},
  instLTNat.lt 0 k →
    instLTNat.lt 0 J →
      ∀ (x y : Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.Numerical k), Exists fun t => Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.allowedIndex x y t

atom_testers : ∀ {k n b degree r : Nat} {hr : instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 2 r) n} (D : Lax342547.ConcreteCut.Testers hr)
  (x : Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.PointAtom k n b degree),
  And (Eq (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe D.role x.profile) (Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.PointAtom.numerical hr x).role)
    (And
      (∀ (t : Lax342547.TagGeometry.Tag k),
        Eq (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe (D.aTag t) x.profile) ((Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.PointAtom.numerical hr x).aTag t))
      (∀ (t : Lax342547.TagGeometry.Tag k),
        Eq (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe (D.bTag t) x.profile) ((Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.PointAtom.numerical hr x).bTag t)))

tester_properties : ∀ {k : Nat},
  And
    (∀ (x y : Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.Numerical k),
      Eq (Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.testerEntry x y) (Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.testerEntry y x))
    (∀ (x : Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.Numerical k), Eq (Lax342547.WitnessAtoms.testerEntry x x) x.role)

proofs.description:
Every failure of column injectivity has a nonzero coefficient relation.
For each relation, its single image is uniform on an affine space whose
translation dimension is at least dim(S). Union over at most 2^|J|
coefficient vectors gives the stated bound.

A left inverse of the nominal coefficient matrix lifts any T-tuple of
common-subspace vectors to the allowed column spaces. Thus the image
contains an injective copy of the full T-fold common subspace.

A new dependence extending an injective fixed map must have a nonzero
coefficient among the random columns. Its image equals a prescribed
negative old image. The affine single-image bound applies to each such
relation; union over old coefficients and nonzero new coefficients.

Apply the exact affine linear-image bound to the independent product of
column translation spaces. The rank estimate is t dim(S), uniformly in
the size t of the nominal tuple and in all column offsets.
The empty-selector coordinate on the chosen block recovers each input bit.

Choose a bit on which the labels differ. The empty-selector equation
gives u+v, and the singleton-selector equation gives s_a u+t_a v.
Their nonzero determinant recovers u and v coordinate by coordinate.

At a fixed selector label, varying one base block changes the point
input by exactly the direction matrix. The constant base coordinate
does not change, so this formula keeps the affine shift explicit.

Separate the tester part from the two ordered mixer sums. The numerical
tester record determines the first part; the ordered product identities
determine the other two exactly.

Only allowed distinct-atom evaluations are tested. Outside the incident
stars both prescribed bits vanish. On the diagonal each ordered product
occurs twice and cancels, so no same-atom evaluations need be prescribed.

On an incident component the atom is its point outer product, and it is
zero on every other component. Pairing two outer products through L and
R factors into their two ordered bilinear evaluations.

Apply the cut map to the representation supported only at l. Its sum
over an unordered pair is the point moment precisely when l is incident.

Each ordinary block is intersected with the allowed tag blocks. The
generic and shared-only flavors retain all common coordinates; a pure
flavor removes just S among those coordinates.

The uniform mass on the finite bit-function space is the product of the
uniform masses of its retained coordinate bits.

Expand the actual individual key span using its at most fourteen
generators. Sparse fresh coefficient extraction kills every base-vector
coefficient, including inactive generators, hence their entire sum.

A primal vector has zero channel projections. In its pin/private
decomposition those projections lie in complementary protected and
private spaces, so both vanish; the channel-supported private vector
is zero and the original vector is in the pin.

Project a barred decomposition onto each primal endpoint. Private
channels project to zero, and unselected sparse supports force both
projected key vectors to vanish. Keys have no channels, hence the
nominal key vector is zero. Protected/private complementarity then
reduces the remaining decomposition to a pin vector.

Project the paired pure annihilator to either individual primal quotient.
Each sign's quotient kernel is a projected pin of dimension at most K
plus at most fourteen selected rays. Sum the two kernel budgets.

Pins project into their stored primal projections, keys project into
the endpoint's selected rays, and every private channel projects to zero.

Each endpoint contributes its two lists, of length at most seven each.
Restricting to incident atoms cannot enlarge their fourteen-vector span.

Choose the independent frozen/table splittings, and precompose both
with primal-preserving retractions onto table plus keys. This keeps
all baseline agreements while bounding its primal channel rank by the
table-primal dimension, number of key directions, and opposite pin rank.

For an opposite channel, its frozen projection is a pin. The baseline
evaluation is the sum of a function of the retracted primal input and
the actual input's pairing with that pin. Factor through the product of
the primal retraction's range and the opposite pin dual, then count its
dimension.

Point moments satisfy symmetry and the binary diagonal identity. Conversely,
expand a matrix in the constant, diagonal, and symmetric off-diagonal
generators. Each generator is a sum of at most four point moments.

Normalize both weights by their sup bounds and apply the uniform rank
estimate. If either bound is zero its weight vanishes identically.

Apply the bilinear estimate separately after each finite conditioning
record. The two coefficient spaces may depend on the record. Sum with
the original nonnegative cell masses, retaining all density costs and
without normalizing discarded mass away.

Group the second weight over the fibers of the matrix's linear map.
Fiberwise Cauchy-Schwarz costs at most 2^(number of columns - rank) in
squared energy. Apply the full dot-product Walsh bound to the resulting
weight on the row-coordinate space.

Multiplying a bounded test weight by a nonnegative relative density
bounded by C multiplies its sup bound by at most C. The two factors
therefore cost C₁C₂, without changing the bilinear rank.

An arbitrary phase depending only on one input group can be absorbed
into that group's weight without changing its absolute value. This
includes all affine terms and any frozen within-group quadratic phases.

Bound each weight's squared energy by the number of inputs. Rank-nullity
cancels the inactive coordinates after normalization, leaving squared
correlation at most 2^(-rank), hence the claimed square-root bound.

Transpose reverses the point-input order. Linearity in the ambient matrix
then identifies the combined matrix with the indexed ordered parity.

Taking the four mixed differences cancels both affine terms and the
constant term. The remaining coefficient is the matrix restricted to the
two flavor direction maps.

The chosen retained block is a submatrix of the actual mixed coefficient
matrix. Taking a submatrix cannot increase rank.

Restricting an ordered evaluation or its reverse gives the two ordered
blocks. Both orders of the self-Gram form vanish on the free directions.

At a fixed label the constant coordinate is unchanged, while each retained
base bit contributes its selector evaluation times that bit.

The two sharp restrictions are the label-weighted matrix and its
transpose. Hence all three nonzero self-Gram parities are retained as
submatrices on every pair of flavors.

Union over the two labels and all forward/reverse coefficient lists.
Each nonempty indexed parity has a uniform free block; for n≥50 its
low-rank probability is at most 2^(-n). No flavor union is needed.

Union over the label pairs and the four ordered self-Gram coefficient
pairs. Each nonzero parity is controlled by either the full uniform
matrix or its uniform disjoint alternating block.

A parity involving an indexed mixer retains its free-direction rank,
even with either self-Gram order added. A parity using only self-Gram
evaluations retains its sharp-direction rank. Every flavor contains
both blocks, so the same choices work for all tags and flavors.

Order the finite atom indices. For the increasing order of each distinct
pair choose one allowed term, with factors one and the desired correction.
All other factors are zero. Exactly one ordered sum contributes; binary
addition cancels the old entry. Diagonal entries are unchanged.

Observe an allowed channel vector only through its pairings with the baseline image. This observation factors through the baseline dual map. A section onto its image therefore gives a projection inside the same allowed value space with rank at most the baseline rank.

Use the full combined primal spaces for both reciprocal baseline maps. Their bounded covector ranks control the two replacement derivatives. Coordinate matrix tests prove that every component response is unchanged for arbitrary input matrices.
Postcompose the derivative map with the allowed value projection. All observed dot products are preserved and the derivative image lies in the bounded-dimensional projection image.
Convert baseline covectors into their coordinate vectors. Coordinate conversion cannot increase rank; apply the allowed derivative replacement to this actual observation map.

Start from the proved unrestricted solution of the actual scalar recipe. Replace its two derivative families with bounded-rank families while preserving the pure response and every derivative contraction. This retains the whole-space linearized solution with the paper baseline rank bound.

Choose the two bounded derivatives independently in every component. The component identities preserve the full response on the actual cut-profile pair space. Both derivative ranks are at most three times the pin budget plus twenty-eight.
Choose a linear section of the observation map onto its range. Composing that section with the observation map preserves all observations and bounds the new image dimension by the observation rank.

Extract the disjoint partition while retaining the original masses.
The absolute reference cap and density bound control each cumulative
new rank. Normalize only at the end, keeping the exact conditional
event bounds, uniform density cost, and pointwise mass recovery.

Evaluation on an opposite channel basis vector reads precisely the
corresponding coordinate of the allowed quotient-map output.

The reciprocal cross form agrees with the actual column table on
pinned inputs. Orthogonal tests kill its protected-channel quotient,
and the second actual injection flag forces the vector to zero.

The domain quotient kills a frozen input. An allowed value pairs to
zero with an opposite protected-channel projection.

A primal embedding has zero channel projection, so every allowed
channel change is zero on that opposite primal argument.

Coordinate duality identifies every functional annihilating the
protected space with a perpendicular channel vector. Double annihilation
therefore detects membership in the protected space.

Every actual pin channel projection lies in its protected channel,
which is killed by the allowed value space.

The reference raw law is a product over components, and so is its channel
pushforward. Multiplying the component bounds gives the paper's fixed
joint density constant 2^(|E|(h²+2)).
Sum the pointwise density bound over any channel event.

The raw mass is constant on each injective Gram orbit and its total
mass is at most one. Independent columns give that orbit mass at least
2^(-h²-2), so the density on every orbit is at most 2^(h²+2).

A paired-frame change carrying one channel pair to the other bijects
their full raw-frame completions, giving exactly equal marginal masses.

Ordinary testers vanish on the common moment space. Shared testers are
summed over an even number of tags. The checked cut-kernel theorem gives
representative independence, and quotient descent constructs the actual
linear functionals on the image of the restricted cut map.

Instantiate the proved binary symmetrization identity with the descended
testers and the actual ordered-component mixer sum.

Every coordinate read by the ordered tester and # forms is unchanged by
the Z-coordinate map. This proves the matrix identity for any linear Z
change, in particular for every invertible one.

The ordered tester form has precisely the tester values on point moments.
The # form vanishes on equal point inputs, since each selector difference
is zero. Linearity extends this equality to their full span.

Construct the descended testers, a frame with the concrete self-Gram

The pin extractor sends each selected key to zero or to the selected
base ray. Quotient its output by that ray, so it kills both the pin and
the full key span and descends through their sum.

On the finite label-coefficient space, a sum lying in the pin has zero
coefficient at the fresh label. Factor its coordinate projection through
the pin quotient and evaluate it on coefficient vectors supported at one label.

Choose a linear section onto the image of the quotient composite. The
kernel condition makes the prescribed output independent of that section.
Extend from the image to the whole quotient vector space.

Restrict the middle map to the image of the right map. Its image is in
the left kernel; restriction costs at most the right-image codimension.

Apply the linear-map bound to the matrix sandwich. Rank-nullity and
invariance under transpose identify its right loss with the second kernel.

The kernel of the left quotient is its subspace. The right quotient's
dual image is its annihilator, whose codimension is the subspace dimension.

The sparse exclusions imply independence of the actual incident key
spans. Their dimensions are at most twenty-eight. Admissibility is
exactly the compatibility needed by the nominal baseline theorem.
Apply it to both cross orientations and assemble the two full forms;
each has both reciprocal rank bounds and retains every frozen entry.

An endpoint-supported nominal primal or channel vector selects exactly
the corresponding P, Q, X, or Y block of the joint observation matrix.

The two channel evaluation maps are Y-transpose P and X-transpose Q.
Their matrix pairing is the original channel trace contraction by cyclic
trace. Sum these identities over the actual component tensors.

If the actual cross Grams extend the whole numerical table, first use
extension independence on effective profiles, then identify the full
contraction with the model's original frame tensor contraction.

Injectivity of the two primal frames recovers each column and row of the
coefficient matrix. Transposing the minus annihilator gives $Y^TP=0$,
which makes every self-contraction vanish.

Multiply the reference certificate union bound by the allowed joint
density. A quarter of DN pays the coefficient count, leaving at least
a quarter of DN of exponential decay after the rank-2D image cost.

Choose one ambient multiplier larger than every fixed linear coefficient
in the image and description costs. Multiplication by n then pays all
four inequalities simultaneously, for every positive n and every D.

The concrete primal-plus-channel dimension is linear in n. Substituting
its exact coefficients gives a scale independent of n and of the unit law.

Common primal images also lie in the two full plus spans. Each common
image lifts to a zero-image relation between the endpoints, so its
intersection dimension is bounded by the nominal relation-kernel dimension.

Every large primal intersection has a bounded-column kernel certificate.
Apply the all-rank reference image cap to each fixed certificate, with
zero minus tuple, and pay the exact number of coefficient descriptions.

Forget the Gram and injectivity constraints and count the four binary
matrices at every component. Each component uses 2N(d+h) bits.

The cardinality of the function space is the product of the cardinalities
of the component spaces. Its uniform mass therefore factors exactly as
the product of the component uniform masses.

The reference pin cap is the checked all-rank raw image cap. Substituting
it in bounded peeling gives a disjoint partition, preserves all initial
images, and bounds the total dimension by the initial rank plus K. The
normalized leaves retain the quantitative joint density and image bounds.

Use the exact metadata/image record count to bound discarded fibers.
On every retained fiber, the unconditional raw reference cap supplies
the fresh peeling with its required all-rank estimate. All old pins and
deliberately added images are preserved within the final total budget.

The effective equation agrees with the full contraction because the
baseline extends the table. On selected atoms the binary gradient
prescriptions agree with the frozen contraction values. Linearity makes
the residual zero on the sum of those two subspaces.

The four row-sum identities at one endpoint are precisely the two-list
self and opposite gradient equations. Enumerate the two possible target
endpoints to identify their prescribed opposite p values.

First construct the compatible symmetric atom matrix from the numerical
role and p data. Then realize its difference from the fixed tester matrix
using one allowed formal ordered L/R product per distinct atom pair.

The two role equations turn the opposite coupled equation into equality
of the cross row totals. The two self totals already equal the prescribed
diagonal sums. Construct the symmetric matrix with those row sums; its
symmetry converts them into exactly the two list-gradient requirements.

Reindex the independent raw draws by component and multiply their exact
image bounds. Both tuple dimensions and ranks may vary arbitrarily with
the component. This gives the finite reference cap with every rank and
conditioning cost explicit, before the final parameter payment.

Disintegrate the actual uniform raw law over its complete plus-frame
observation. Each fiber is the independent product of the checked minus
completion laws. Multiply its uniform joint-minus image bound by the
plus-prescription probability and integrate. The result has factor 4^k
and dimension loss k(d+h), uniformly over both nominal tuple ranks.

Extract independent nominal image bases from both tested coefficient
tuples. The original exact-image event implies these basis prescriptions,
so the cap depends on the true nominal ranks even for dependent tuples.

Use a basis of each component/sign pin space and its stored exact images.
These coefficient matrices have precisely the pin dimensions as their
nominal ranks. The all-rank image theorem applies to the same event.

The list labels are injective, so their sum is the sum over the selected
label set. The common scalar identifies each selected block with the
corresponding atom. The finite intersection/difference identity deletes
exactly those blocks from every component.

Choose the scalar decompositions at both endpoints and subtract their
actual selected atoms. Pure annihilation is preserved, and deleting the
selected labels preserves the label and sum-of-ranks budgets and all
Boolean moment identities of the surviving base blocks.
The finite-dimensional double-annihilator theorem identifies the response range with every target functional vanishing on its coannihilator. Membership in the actual range supplies parameters.
The pure quotient family and both allowed derivative families are additive in their parameters. Coordinate matrix pairing and both channel contractions are additive in the appropriate argument.
Scalar multiplication of all three parameter families scales the full response. This proves homogeneity on the actual pair of cut profiles.
Use the proved full obstruction decomposition. The remainder lies in the effective profile space and the selected part lies in the endpoint atom span.

The actual scalar recipe, frozen baseline and selected gradient prescriptions make both endpoint residuals vanish on their correct spaces. The proved obstruction reduction and duality construct a full response realizing this actual recipe residual.
Each selected witness is one of the endpoint atoms. The finite linear combination therefore belongs to the selected-atom span in the correct space.
Package the pure and derivative families into a product module and prove their response map linear using the checked additivity and homogeneity. Apply double annihilation to its actual range.

Every full obstruction belongs to the correct spaces at both endpoints. The target vanishes there, so double annihilation yields an unrestricted pure and derivative response realizing it on the whole actual profile-pair space.

Use the combined retained mass to bound discarded weight. Every retained
leaf has a positive restriction mass, and its normalization preserves all
quotient-rank image tests with the stated loss. Retain exact weighted
recovery and the explicit absolute joint density factor.

The residual budget for a fresh peeling is relative to its part. Summing
with the actual part weights gives the same budget for the whole mixture.

Factor the row map through its image. Pullback along the resulting
surjection preserves rank, because its dual is injective. The only
loss is restriction to the image, which costs at most twice its
codimension.

Restricting the domain loses at most the subspace codimension. Restricting
the output functional to that subspace loses at most the dimension of
its annihilator, which is the same codimension. Rank-nullity combines
the two losses.

Three independent sample positions would produce three pairwise holes.
This argument does not require the sampled raw vertices to be distinct.

The ceiling of the new-rank allowance costs less than one extra dimension.
For zeta at most one, the paper's final budget absorbs this and all old
and deliberately added pins, with uniform slack.

A retained record has positive mass, so choose a consistent point to join
its image pins to the old pins. The normalized fiber has the absolute D'
density bound. Apply bounded peeling on its full support, count only new
quotient dimensions, and charge them to the final total budget.

Adjoin the endpoint's at most fourteen key labels to the component's
support. Actual list freshness identifies the only key at the selected
label; it spans the selected affine ray exactly on its incident star.

Project the nominal pure annihilator to this endpoint. Extract the
selected label in both factors. Its base moment is killed by its affine
ray quotients, or by no rays off its star, giving a scalar point or zero.

Apply the component theorem to the actual pair of cut profiles and the
entrywise reconstruction supplied by their low-rank label decomposition.

Expand the sandwich entrywise. On the diagonal symmetry cancels its
two mixed terms; the Boolean square and moment diagonal identity force
the constant row to be the selected affine vector times the constant
entry. Substitution in every entry leaves only its point moment.

Subtracting the constant-coordinate multiple of the affine point has
kernel exactly its ray; the point's constant coordinate is one.

In incident components the selected atom contracts to a bilinear test
of its two nominal key vectors. Both are zero in the barred quotients.
All other components of the atom are zero.

Expand the endpoint tuple into coordinate singletons, then use linearity
and the selected-atom test on every term of the finite sums.

Each response is linear, so subtracting the selected part preserves
its zero value on the original pure obstruction.

Use the checked selected-block theorem in every component of the actual
pure obstruction, pad absent labels by zero, and apply scalar consistency.

The actual representative gives the three-edge cut relation. Reconstruct
its three components and separate their union of at most 3R labels.

Choose the checked component label decompositions of the actual pure
obstruction. Their degree margin permits triangle interpolation. Every
fresh selected witness then has its own scalar, shared across its star.

Read the affine constant entry of each selected block. Its triangle
relations and off-star vanishing give a common scalar, which recovers
the entire selected base moment on every component.

Fix one edge from the selected tag. A triangle through any other edge
has zero on its off-star edge, so its two star coefficients agree.

For each label, a product of affine bit functions singles it out among the
specified labels. Its degree is at most their number minus one. Applying
these separating polynomials to a linear relation recovers every coefficient.

Prescribe the chosen forward block and set its reverse to zero. Disjoint
index sets make these prescriptions consistent, so the alternating-block
observation is a surjective linear map and hence has the uniform law.

Use the disjoint even and odd indices for a square block of side floor(n/2).
Its rank cannot exceed the rank of the alternating matrix, and its uniform
law satisfies the rectangular low-rank probability bound.

Push the uniform family of sharp mixers through its nonzero label-weighted
sum. The forward and reverse ranks obey the square-matrix count; their
alternating sum obeys the disjoint-block count proved above.

Distinct labels differ in some bit, so their coefficient sum at that bit
is nonzero in the binary field. The weighted matrix map is surjective.

All tester and sharp coordinates vanish on a free Z-direction input.
Consequently an optional self-Gram evaluation contributes zero to the
free-direction block used to test a nonempty mixer parity.

The ordinary and shared testers vanish on sharp directions. Evaluating
the remaining form gives the selector sum s_a+t_a multiplying M_a.
Apply the bilinear form to basis vectors to recover the whole matrix block.

The bit matrix pairs equal bit coordinates. Interchanging the finite
sums gives the specified linear combination of the vector-slot dot products.

The image of the bit matrix is linearly equivalent to N independent
copies of the coefficient matrix's image. Dimensions add over that
finite product, giving the exact bit rank.

A nonzero coefficient matrix has rank at least one, so the full bit
form has rank at least N. The general bilinear Walsh estimate gives the
required correlation bound, uniformly in the two bounded group weights.

On each leaf a pinned input has its stored image. Substituting that image
in each cross orientation leaves a condition on the other unit alone.
If both inputs are pinned, the two substitutions give the same numerical
test, so no additional joint orientation filter is necessary.

Use the actual joint plus/minus frame observations at both endpoints.
Their exact-pin events give the fixed images required by the separation
theorem, with no independence assumption on the endpoints of a unit.

Use the checked exact count of selector/base coordinates to specialize
the linear-size scale choice to the paper's actual coefficient space.
This single ambient scale works for every positive n and every unit law.

The paper's early constants satisfy the strict-majority condition and
specialize the per-representation support bound to 16000 tags.

The coefficient-count union estimate bounds the actual joint-capped law's
intersection exception. Outside it, injective tensor rank preservation,
cyclic majority normalization, and the concrete trace identity give all
the rank, support, uniqueness, and chiStar assertions of Lemma 4.4.

Adjoin the at most fourteen key labels to the sparse support and extract
each fresh key coefficient through the pin quotient. The unselected
support contributes zero, and list injectivity isolates the tested key.

Choose independent sparse vectors spanning all sparse members of each
projected space, and collect their labels. Interpolation makes every
comparison with another sparse expansion unique, so that expansion has
no additional nonzero labels. The union over signs and components has
the required size.

Each nonzero cut matrix has rank at least one. Sum this inequality
over the unordered components, counting the zero matrices as zero.

Apply majority normalization to an actual restricted cut representative.
The cyclic majority-intersection theorem supplies exactly the subspace
condition required to translate its majority value to zero.

The trace identity and concrete self-Gram identity equate eta on every
component of the two shared tensors. The eta-valued representatives
therefore differ by a constant. Their majority zero sets intersect,
forcing that constant to vanish before summing the values over tags.

The intersection bound controls both total profile ranks. Normalize each
profile, retain its support bound, and apply the shared-trace conclusion.

A single ambient scale paying twice the metadata coefficient leaves a
uniform exponentially small discarded fraction, independent of the law.

The record count is at most 2^(a n + u N). Multiplying by the cutoff
2^(-(u+1)N) leaves the exact metadata cost 2^(a n - N).

Charge the preceding retained leaf fraction and the retained metadata
fiber separately. Their two exact normalization costs fit inside D'.

The discarded points are covered by small fibers, each of mass below the
threshold. A finite union bound pays the number of possible split records.

Choose a rank-r symmetric factorization for each matrix. Its two factors
encode the original matrix and use |I|r+r² binary entries.

Factor M through its rank and take a left inverse U of the first factor Z.
Put H=UMUᵀ. The projection ZU fixes M on the left and, by symmetry, on
the right, proving ZHZᵀ=M. The rank of M forces H to be nonsingular.

Subtract the diagonal in characteristic two. The desired remaining row
sums total zero, and a symmetric star at one index realizes them with
zero diagonal. Add the prescribed diagonal back.

Use one distinguished row and column. They carry the requested column
and row sums, and their common entry corrects the shared total.

Construct the two symmetric diagonal blocks from the self-sum conditions
and the cross block from the equality of its row and column totals.
Its transpose gives the reverse block, so the full matrix has exactly
the required diagonal and both list sums of every row.

The full channel maps restrict to the two table evaluations on the
projected primal factors. Extension independence of each tensor
contraction therefore gives equality on every effective component.
Summing gives the asserted identity on the entire effective profile.

Every component/sign pin space has dimension at most the total pin
budget. Pad one of its bases to K vectors, giving a uniform coefficient
array whose span recovers that precise nominal subspace.

The padded record has one bit per component, sign, basis index, endpoint,
and primal-or-channel coordinate. Count these independent binary slots.

Each bilinear form is determined by a matrix with one entry per pair of
basis vectors. Both table domains have dimension at most 2K+2h. Multiply
the binary matrix counts over both cross orientations and all components.

Admissibility already fixes every pinned-primal versus channel entry;
no agreement on the unpinned channel-by-channel block is needed.

Each primal projection of a stored pin belongs to the corresponding
projected space, by its defining image witness.

The projected protected channel space has a linear complement in the
channel coordinate space. No orthogonal-complement assumption is made.

Channel projection cannot increase dimension. Sum this inequality over
the component/sign spaces of the fixed endpoint.

Read a table vector in its two primal and two channel coordinate blocks.
This map is injective. Each primal projection has dimension at most the
total pin rank, and each channel block has its full coordinate dimension.

Enlarging stored pins enlarges every primal projection, hence the full
table-coordinate space, while retaining all channel coordinates.

Each ordinary block is allowed at at most k tags. A set of more than k
tags therefore forbids each ordinary block somewhere. The coordinate
projection theorem identifies the resulting intersection of moment spaces.

Test every product of quotient functionals. Double annihilation puts the
contracted tensor in the left subspace; the two-quotient rank theorem
then bounds its rank. Coordinate duality preserves the original rank.

Every row of each quotient-killing matrix is a quotient functional.
Their product test is precisely the corresponding sandwich entry.

The explicit affine-ray projection kills exactly the selected ray.
Pure annihilation therefore kills its tensor sandwich, and the moment
identities reduce the block to its selected point moment.

Expand the base matrix in elementary outer products. Each lifted outer
product contracts to the bilinear form evaluated on its two lifted factors.

Pull each base quotient form back through the two extractors. All label
blocks except the selected one vanish, so the original annihilation
tests give every base quotient test of the selected block.

The matrix of the pulled-back channel dot product evaluates on an outer
product as that bilinear form on its two generating vectors.

The chosen ambient extensions agree with their original maps on the two
factor spaces, so their outer-product contraction is the required dot product.

Extend the proposed functional linearly to all matrices. Its values on
the outer-product generators agree with the constructed contraction,
which determines its restriction to their span uniquely.

Any two ambient extensions agree on every generating outer product.
Linearity extends this equality to the whole projected tensor space.

An injective linear map identifies every subspace with its image, so
left multiplication preserves column rank. Transposition gives the
corresponding assertion for right multiplication by the dual frame.

Both tensor descriptions have the same rank, and the shared tensor's
column space is contained in both endpoint spans.

Apply the shared-tensor rank bound independently in every component
and add the resulting nonnegative integer inequalities.

Cyclic trace moves the two frame maps together. Their product is the
transpose of the prescribed self-Gram matrix, giving its entrywise
pairing with the coefficient matrix.

Every formal block has a nonsingular middle matrix. Their polar maps
are jointly injective. Counting the two row halves, the two orders,
the J mixer copies, and the incident components gives the exact rank.

Pairing l with another tag is a bijection from the tags different
from l to the two-element components incident to l.

Expand the atom's incident components in the two orders of the mixer
sum. The symmetric component factorization turns each forward or
reverse contribution into precisely its indexed formal product.

The row space is the image of the dual row map. Its dimension is at
most the formal row dimension, which is 4J(2k) times the total factor
rank. This bound is independent of n.

Substituting a row map whose image has codimension at most s loses
at most 2s from the exact formal polar rank.

The tester term is constant along the free Z block. The point input
changes affinely by its direction matrix, and the indexed row map is
linear. Combining these facts with the concrete mixer expansion gives
the claimed affine substitution with an explicitly fixed linear part.

Equality on the fixed row space means every functional on the formal
row vectors has the same value. The dual separates points, so the row
vectors agree. Their affine quadratic evaluations therefore agree.

Apply the four-term binary polar operator to the actual atom test.
Its affine expansion cancels both the constant tester value and the
non-Z shift, leaving exactly the formal polar form pulled back along
the fixed Z row map.

The actual atom test has the polar matrix of the affine formal
quadratic. Its rank is the rank of the pulled-back polar map, so the
formal substitution estimate applies directly to the actual Z bits.

A nonzero profile has positive total factor rank, and a positive k
gives incident components at every tag. The exact formal rank is at
least 2J. Losing at most twice the Z row codimension proves the unary
lower bound, uniformly over the fixed non-Z values.

Use the explicit threshold, independent of n and of the tester family.
The finite union bound then yields mixers satisfying every unary test
for each n above that threshold, before any unit law is introduced.

If every mixer choice failed, the bad event would be the whole finite
probability space and would have mass one. The explicit union bound
below one therefore leaves a simultaneous successful choice.

Choose simultaneous successful unary mixers above the explicit
threshold. For each profile, tag, and label, use its factorization to
define the bounded row space before any non-Z values are specified.
The row-space dependence and polar-rank bound then hold for every
allowed fixing with that same space.

Separate the profile-count exponent into its constant part and its slope
in n. The unary corank exponent exceeds that slope by at least one,
leaving the explicit constant threshold times 2^(-n).

Substitute the proved coordinate count. The numerator is C times
2^(a n), with C independent of n and a the displayed profile-count
slope. The denominator exponent is at least (a+1)n. For n≥C, the
elementary inequality n<2^n makes the resulting bound strictly below one.

Take the finite union over the actual low-rank profile space, tags,
and labels. The profile-count bound controls the number of tests, and
each event already includes every fixing of the non-Z coordinates.

For each profile, tag, and label, its symmetric component factorization
determines a bounded row space before any non-Z fixing. The good event
supplies all polar-rank bounds and the factorization supplies dependence
only on those rows, for that same already chosen mixer family.

Joint observations of all independent L and R matrices have total
compatibility codimension at most 2J(Σr)². Selecting the incident row
entries is surjective on the unconstrained lists and cannot increase
codimension. The uniform linear-image bound gives the claimed density.

Multiplication by the packed matrix is exactly the formal row map,
followed by the linear equivalence flattening its indexed row halves.
That equivalence preserves the image dimension.

Sum the joint density domination over the corank event and apply the
checked uniform row-relation bound. The number of formal rows is at
most 4J times the incidence count times K, giving the stated exponent.

Factor each actual symmetric profile component through its rank. The
always-retained free block gives injective direction columns. If any
non-Z fixing fails the unary rank bound, the common row map must have
corank at least s₀+1. The single row-corank event therefore controls all
fixings at once, without a union over their values or over flavors.

Instantiate the simultaneous theorem with the paper's mixer parameters.
For every sufficiently large n it supplies all unary row-space and
polar-rank conclusions and every ordered binary parity bound, before
any unit law is quantified over.

The unary and indexed-binary bad events share the same matrix-family
probability space. Their sum is at most (C_unary+C_binary)/2^n<1 above
the stated threshold. Choose a family outside their union, then choose
sharp matrices outside their own bad event. Restriction to the always
retained blocks supplies every flavor's binary bound for these choices.

All factors in the paper's displayed A are natural numbers, so 4⌈A⌉
is 40(K+1)p_*(g²+5). This exceeds the profile-count slope. Taking J to
be 101(s₀+K²+1) gives the paper's strict mixer-budget inequality.

Apply finite Cauchy-Schwarz to one weight and the Walsh transform of the
other, then substitute the exact transform energy identity.

Compose the nontrivial real binary character with the linear functional.
Its being the trivial character would force the functional to vanish,
so the finite additive-character orthogonality theorem gives zero sum.

The product of the two signs is the character indexed by x+z.
It is trivial exactly when x=z in the binary vector space.

Absorb each subprobability mass into its bounded weight. Its squared
energy is at most its point-mass cap times its total mass, hence at most
the cap. The squared Walsh bound and a square root give Lemma 4.6(b).

Expand the square and interchange the three finite sums. Orthogonality
kills every off-diagonal pair and contributes exactly 2^d on the diagonal.

Every tag has 2k incident components. Choose one for each star and any
of the J mixer copies to obtain an allowed ordered product index.

The actual descended tester evaluations on a point atom are precisely
the sums and tag-dependent shared bit in its numerical tester record.

The cross tester terms occur with their transposes. They cancel on the
diagonal in characteristic two, and each binary role bit squares to itself.
